name: ai-coding-agent-toolkit
description: Production-ready coding standards and config for AI coding agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenCode, and the open AGENTS.md standard) for backend-heavy full-stack developers.

installGroups.general: Cross-stack rules, commands, and agents installed regardless of --stacks filter (coding style, git workflow, testing, security, databases, infra, all slash commands, all agents)
installGroups.java-springboot: Java 17 + Spring Boot 3 rules and skills
installGroups.python-fastapi: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + AI/ML rules and skills
installGroups.ai-ml: RAG/agent/MCP skill packs not tied to a specific language stack

installScopes.global: Default. Installs to ~/.claude (all projects) plus ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/.mcp.json.
installScopes.local: Opt-in via --local/-Local. Installs to ./.claude in the current repo, plus ./CLAUDE.md (from the blank project template, not the personal one) and ./.mcp.json at the project root.

aiTargets.claude: Default. Full install: rules, commands, agents, skills, hooks, MCP config, CLAUDE.md.
aiTargets.copilot: Flattens the selected rules into .github/copilot-instructions.md at the project root.
aiTargets.agentsmd: Flattens the selected rules into AGENTS.md at the project root — the open AGENTS.md standard, read by OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, Google Jules, Zed, Warp, Aider, goose, Amp, and used as a fallback by Cursor/Windsurf/Copilot too.
aiTargets.cursor: Writes one .cursor/rules/<id>.mdc per selected rule, with alwaysApply: true frontmatter.
aiTargets.windsurf: Writes one .windsurf/rules/<id>.md per selected rule; warns if a file exceeds Windsurf's ~6000-char-per-file guidance.
aiTargets.opencode: Writes AGENTS.md (same as agentsmd) plus maps commands to .opencode/command/*.md (as-is, same $ARGUMENTS convention) and agents to .opencode/agent/*.md (mode: subagent; model/tools fields dropped since OpenCode's model ids differ from Claude's).

aiTargetsNote: Every non-claude target skips skills, hooks, and MCP config (no equivalent in v1 — a documented gap, not a silent drop) and always writes to the current directory regardless of --local/global, since none of these tools have a global/user-level config the way Claude Code does. Plain ChatGPT (not Codex) has no repo-level instructions file at all, so there is no --ai=chatgpt target.
